h1: Brewmaster, head brewer or production manager: the titles explained
title: Brewery Job Titles Explained | Craft Beer School
desc: What brewmaster, head brewer, production manager and other brewery job titles mean in practice and how they differ in India.
teaser: The same job can carry three titles in three breweries. Here is what each one usually means.
standfirst: Brewery job titles are not standard. A brewmaster at one brewpub does the same work as a head brewer down the road. This guide explains what each title usually means and how to read a job advert.
sections:
Brewing has no single licensing body that sets job titles, so each brewery names roles to suit itself. A small brewpub may call its only brewer the brewmaster. A large plant may have a head brewer who never touches a mash paddle and a brewing manager who reports to them. The title tells you less than the job description does.

Still, the titles follow a rough pattern. Once you know it, adverts in India start to make sense.

Traditionally a brewmaster is a senior brewer with formal training and years of experience, the person whose judgement sets recipes and standards. In Germany the word Braumeister is a formal qualification earned after training and exams. Elsewhere, including India, it is often used more loosely.

In Indian brewpubs the brewmaster is usually the person in charge of brewing: recipes, raw material orders, the brewing team and beer quality. In some places it is the only brewer on the payroll. Read the advert for team size before you assume seniority.

The head brewer runs the brewing side day to day. They plan the brew schedule, write or adapt recipes, manage assistant brewers, check every tank and sign off beer before it goes to the bar or the packaging line. In most craft breweries the head brewer is the senior technical person and the title means the same as brewmaster.

In a large brewery a head brewer may manage a team of shift brewers and focus on planning, people and quality, with little hands-on brewing.

A production manager looks after the whole plant output, not only the beer recipes. That means brewing, cellar, filtration and packaging as one system: staffing rosters, maintenance windows, raw material stock, yields and cost per litre. They answer to the business for volume and efficiency.

In a brewpub the head brewer usually does this job without the title. In a packaging brewery it is often a separate role, sometimes filled by an engineer rather than a brewer.
The other titles you will see

• Assistant brewer: the entry role on the brewing side. Cleaning, cellar work, brew day tasks under supervision. See our guide to the assistant brewer job.
  • Shift brewer: runs the brewhouse or cellar for a shift in a larger plant.
  • Cellar operator: fermentation and conditioning tanks, transfers, dry hopping and yeast handling.
  • Packaging operator or lead: the canning, bottling or kegging line.
  • QC technician or quality manager: lab testing and the quality system.
  • Brewing consultant: an outside expert who sets up or fixes breweries on contract.
How titles change as a brewery grows

Titles often track the size of the business. A new brewpub opens with one brewer who does everything and may be called brewmaster to impress guests. When the brewery adds a second outlet or a packaging line, that person becomes head brewer with an assistant or two. When volume grows again, the business hires a production manager to run rosters, maintenance and cost, so the head brewer can concentrate on beer.

Some breweries go the other way and keep one senior person responsible for everything with an inflated title. Neither approach is wrong. What matters for you is whether the job gives you room to learn and a clear next step. Ask in the interview who held the role before and where they went next. The answer tells you more than the title on the offer letter.
How to read a job advert

Ignore the title at first and look for three things. How many people does the role manage? Who does it report to? What is the brewhouse size? A head brewer on a 5 hectolitre brewpub kit with one assistant is a hands-on job. A head brewer at a plant with packaging lines is a management job.

Then look at the tasks. If the advert mentions excise registers, raw material purchase and stock, the role carries business responsibility as well as brewing. If it lists only brewing and cleaning, it is a production role whatever it is called. Our overview of jobs in a brewery shows how the roles connect.

Whichever title you aim for, the common ground is the same: you need to understand what happens in the mash, the kettle and the fermenter well enough to explain it to someone else.
faqs: Is a brewmaster more senior than a head brewer?
Not always. In many Indian brewpubs the two titles mean the same job. In larger breweries a brewmaster may sit above the head brewer, but it depends on the company.
Does a production manager need to be a brewer?
Not necessarily. Many production managers are engineers or operations people. In a small brewery the head brewer usually does the job as well.
What title should a beginner apply for?
Assistant brewer, cellar operator or packaging operator. These roles teach the process from the floor up and lead to head brewer in time.
